observations.code_quote:
"description": "Replace the rules of a feature flag whose `filters.version` is 2. Requires the flag's numeric ID; use `feature-flag-get-definition-by-key` to get it from a key. For a flag without `filters.version` 2, use `update-feature-flag` instead; this tool cannot convert a flag between the two formats.

Read the flag first with `feature-flag-get-definition` or `feature-flag-get-definition-by-key`. Build the new `filters` from what you read and send the whole document: `version` 2, the same `return_type`, `default_value` and the complete ordered `rules` list. The server replaces the stored `filters` with what you send, so a rule you leave out is deleted. Rules are evaluated in order and the first rule that returns a value wins.

Each rule you read has an `id`, and randomized rules (`percentage_rollout`, `experiment`) have a `seed`. Send both unchanged on every rule you keep, edit or move, so the rule keeps its identity and nobody is reassigned. Leave `id` and `seed` off a new rule; the server assigns them. Never invent an `id` or change a `seed`: the write is refused.

Send the flag's top-level `version` from your read (not `filters.version`). Returns 409 when the flag changed after that version, and writes nothing. Read the flag again, rebuild the change on the current rules and send it with the new `version`. Do not retry with the same `version`.

Returns 400 naming the first invalid field when the document is invalid. Fix it and send the document again; the next attempt can name another field. Returns 400 with code `reserved_config_version` ("filters.version is reserved") when this project or this flag does not accept version 2 rule changes. Do not remove `filters.version`. Report that to the user; do not work around it with `update-feature-flag`. This tool changes only `filters`. Use `feature-flag-enable` and `feature-flag-disable` to turn the flag on or off.",
